title: Serrated Polyposis Syndrome: A Review and Consensus Statement by the US Multi-Society Task Force on Colorectal Cancer.
authors: Rex DK, Anderson JC, Burke CA, Jacobson BC, May FP, Patel SG, et al.
abstract: Serrated polyposis syndrome (SPS) is the most common polyposis syndrome, yet SPS often goes unrecognized. SPS diagnosis is based on clinical criteria established by the World Health Organization and includes the size, cumulative lifetime number, and location of serrated polyps throughout the colon. Individuals with SPS have an increased risk of prevalent and incident colorectal cancer (CRC). Meticulous inspection, clearing of the colon and frequent surveillance colonoscopy is recommended to decrease incident CRC. Colorectal surgery is indicated for individuals diagnosed with cancer or whose polyp burden cannot be managed endoscopically by expert endoscopists. There is no common germline pathogenic variant associated with SPS. Germline genetic testing is indicated only in individuals who meet criteria for a known hereditary syndrome in the appropriate clinical setting. First-degree relatives of patients with SPS are at heightened risk of CRC and should undergo colonoscopic screening.
cn_title: 美国多学会工作组：锯齿状息肉综合征综述与共识声明
insight: 系统梳理SPS诊断标准、监测与手术指征，强调其作为最常见息肉综合征却常被漏诊，对肠癌筛查与遗传风险评估具有直接指导意义。
grade_rationale: 美国多学会工作组共识声明，虽非RCT但具权威规范性与实践指导力，可能改变SPS筛查与监测策略。

title: Consensus recommendations for the management of locally advanced rectal cancer.
authors: Hofheinz RD, Garcia-Carbonero R, Ciardiello F, Hamilton L, O'Donovan P, Perry R, et al.
abstract: Locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) considerably impairs quality of life (QoL) and compromises prognosis. Immunotherapy induces complete responses in most patients with mismatch repair deficient/microsatellite instability-high (dMMR/MSI-h) LARC, enabling organ preservation; however, challenges include access and inconsistent guideline recommendations. This Delphi study aimed to understand the unmet needs of patients with dMMR/MSI-h LARC and seek recommendations for appropriate diagnosis and management. Europe-based clinical experts participated in a double-blinded modified Delphi panel, with two online surveys and a virtual consensus meeting. Consensus was defined as ≥80% rating their agreement or disagreement on a 9-point Likert scale. Overall, 26 experts participated in the panel surveys, with 15 also participating in the final consensus meeting. Consensus was reached that dMMR/MSI-h LARC substantially affects QoL and a multidisciplinary team is needed for diagnosis, treatment planning, reflex mismatch repair/MSI testing, and staging. Panelists reached consensus that immunotherapy is an efficacious standard of care, offering high complete response rates, a favorable safety profile, and improved QoL. Consensus was also reached that unmet needs include long-term clinical data and biomarkers to predict treatment response and monitor for disease recurrence. Varied reimbursement policies across Europe underscore the need for updated guidelines and broader immunotherapy access. Management recommendations include standardized use of immunotherapy as the preferred treatment approach due to its tolerability and efficacy. This informs the future treatment landscape direction and supports the need for long-term clinical data on immunotherapy use.
cn_title: 局部晚期直肠癌管理共识推荐：dMMR/MSI-h免疫治疗与器官保留
insight: 该Delphi共识明确免疫治疗为dMMR/MSI-h局部晚期直肠癌的首选策略，推动器官保留；提示肠癌肝转移需关注MSI状态检测及免疫治疗长期数据。
grade_rationale: 基于欧洲多国专家改良Delphi共识，虽非RCT但直接指导dMMR/MSI-h LARC的临床决策，具有实践改变潜力。

title: Individual and Occupational Factors Associated with Receipt of Guideline-Concordant Cancer Screening in California Firefighters.
authors: Gabriel J, Urwin D, Nguyen TT, Rohlf E, Glenn BA, Fejerman L, et al.
journal: Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention : a Publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, Cosponsored By the American Society of Preventive Oncology
abstract: Firefighters face elevated cancer risk due to occupational exposures, yet cancer screening adherence and associated factors remain poorly characterized. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of survey data from 3,076 active-duty career firefighters in California without a prior cancer diagnosis. Screening adherence was evaluated against U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) and National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) guidelines for colorectal (CRC), breast, cervical, prostate, skin, and lung cancer. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the associations between screening receipt and demographic, occupational, behavioral, clinical, and health belief factors. Overall, screen-eligible participants were racially/ethnically diverse (25% Hispanic; 37% non-White), had a mean age of 41 years, and a mean tenure in the fire service of 17 years. Receipt of guideline-concordant screening varied by cancer type and guideline: CRC (54% NFPA, 68% USPSTF), breast (76%), cervical (75%), prostate (59% NFPA, 78% USPSTF), skin (29%), and lung (ever low-dose computed tomography, 10%). Older age (odds ratio [OR]=1.19-2.65 per 5 years), 1+ years since a routine doctor's visit (OR=0.36-0.58), and family history of cancer (OR=1.33-1.77) were consistently associated with receipt of cancer screening. Firefighters who were younger (yet within eligibility age range), had not recently engaged in routine healthcare, and did not have a family history of cancer were less likely to be screened. This is the first broad characterization of cancer screening among career firefighters, identifying potentially actionable targets for interventions to close screening gaps in this high-risk population.
cn_title: 加州职业消防员癌症筛查依从性及其个体与职业相关因素分析
insight: 首次系统刻画职业消防员多癌种筛查依从性，结直肠癌筛查率仅54%-68%；提示高危职业人群需针对性干预以缩小筛查缺口。
grade_rationale: 横断面调查设计、单一人群、无纵向结局，证据等级有限，但为高危职业人群筛查干预提供靶点，尚不足以直接改变临床实践。

title: Yield of actionable variants from high-risk cancer gene panel testing in guideline-eligible and ineligible individuals.
authors: Lee SS, Zhang J, Bristow SL, Rojahn S, Mackall M, Malhotra M, et al.
abstract: Hereditary cancer testing can identify individuals with a significant risk of cancer, and provide an opportunity for early risk management, prevention, precision treatment strategies, and family cascade testing. Medical professional organizations have developed guidance on genetic testing criteria based on personal and family histories. However, many individuals with cancer-predisposing pathogenic germline variants remain unidentified. The objective of this study was to determine the utility of a multi-cancer, clinically actionable cancer syndrome gene panel in identifying pathogenic variants among individuals both meeting and not meeting national genetic testing criteria. This retrospective cohort study analyzed 153,767 unrelated consecutive women and men, unselected for personal or family cancer history, who were referred for genetic testing across multiple sites from June 2020 to August 2023. Positivity rates were evaluated and compared according to testing guideline eligibility and cancer site-specific recommended gene sets. In a multi-cancer panel of 29 clinically actionable genes, pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in 6.5% of individuals meeting hereditary testing criteria and 4.8% of those not meeting criteria. Overall, 22% of individuals with positive findings would have been missed had guideline-informed testing criteria been used, suggesting substantial missed diagnostic and therapeutic opportunities. Gene-level analyses revealed higher positivity rates for These findings indicate that strict testing criteria may miss 22% of individuals with an actionable hereditary cancer gene variant. The use of comprehensive multi-cancer panels, alongside broader eligibility criteria, can identify individuals with hereditary cancer syndromes and improve opportunities for targeted screening, clinical management, and cascade testing for relatives.
cn_title: 多癌种可操作基因panel检测在符合与不符合指南标准人群中的阳性检出率
insight: 严格遵循指南标准会漏诊22%的可操作遗传性肿瘤变异，提示肠癌遗传筛查应放宽标准并采用多基因panel，以捕获更多林奇综合征等可干预人群。
grade_rationale: 基于15万余人大型回顾性队列，证实指南标准漏诊率高，对遗传筛查策略有直接实践改变潜力。
